page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual machine hosted on KVM hypervisors. The instance is provisioned with 4 shared vCPUs mapped to an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The host configuration incorporates 50 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address. Accelerated instruction sets are present, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as hardware cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA. No dedicated graphics acceleration is bundled.

Benchmark data displays strong single-threaded CPU capability alongside moderate multi-threaded efficiency. The instance achieved 2758.58 in stress-ng single-core performance and 33.57 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, both positioning in the top quartile. Geekbench scores registered 1840.0 for single-core and 5516.0 for multi-core processing, while PassMark returned a CPU score of 9273.65. Redis operations demonstrated stable throughput at 6.19 million SET operations per second, and static web serving reached 9.12 GB/sec. A notable hardware constraint appears in memory subsystem testing, where large-block uncached read bandwidth measured 6.32 GB/sec, reflecting shared-resource memory limitations under heavy data movement.

Given its balanced ratio of memory to compute and reliable single-core speed, the instance is well suited for web hosting, staging environments, Redis caching nodes, and continuous integration runners. Tasks dependent on high uncached memory throughput or sustained non-shared CPU execution represent the primary operational tradeoffs.
